decision: The site is a designed static website from tad data - minimal, elegant, no JavaScript - not a tad text page.
why: It is the observatory's visit card.
rejected: Rendering tad's own pages for the observatory.

decision: Discovery is hexagonal; on GitHub the mark is the oco-project topic plus a kind topic, confirmed by oco.toml.
why: Topics are what GitHub's search indexes best: one query finds every marked repository.
rejected: Code search for oco.toml (slow, rate-limited) as the primary way.

decision: The observatory's engine (mark, discovery, harvest, site) is its own repository, in Rust; tad is to be rewritten in Rust with its formats unchanged.
why: Sturdier machinery, compiled checks, one toolchain across the commons' tools.

decision: Everything thought, decided and planned is written into the tad structure - concepts, decisions, backlog, session log, milestones - in the project it belongs to.
why: Nothing may depend on anyone remembering.
rejected: Prose documents alone; plans kept in conversation or memory.

decision: The observatory is a meta structure, tied to no project; its tabs are itself and the grand projects, each with its own views.
why: A devices tab made the whole look device-centred; devices are one part of one grand project.
rejected: One flat set of tabs for everything.

decision: The ecosystem of gathering, reflection and propagation is called oco-eco (observation commons observatory ecosystem).
why: It has become an information ecosystem, and deserves a name.

decision: The working practices are tad data in the observatory, and every agent reads them live through lab-agent guide.
why: An improvement made once reaches every agent; no agent depends on its own memory to work well.
rejected: Practices kept only in one agent's memory or in prose files that drift.

decision: Table columns are ranked best first from the data; unknown is shown as unknown and never counted as failure.
why: The order corrects itself as support grows; a gap in knowledge is not a verdict.
rejected: Hand-ordered columns; one 'how close' percentage that counted unknown as zero.

decision: tad is not a template but a rhizoid module (a rhizcut) supplied in every repository, with standard gatherers (CI jobs and hooks reading real files, tests, releases); tad has its own path, shown among the other projects rather than as a top tab.
why: Templates and copied subtrees drift and cannot send fixes back; tad is central but smaller than a grand aim like Linux Phones.
rejected: tad as a template or a subtree copy; tad as a top tab.

decision: Projects are shown against three horizons - working, perfection, ongoing perfection - on the readiness ladder, with milestones whose criteria are measured data.
why: Overall progress alone loses the reader; three honest horizons show where a project really stands.
rejected: A single progress bar; milestones ticked by hand.
